docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🔒 Privacy-First: 100% local processing, zero cloud dependencies
  • 🤖 AI-Powered: Uses local LLMs for intelligent file organization
  • 🎯 Methodologies: Supports PARA, Johnny Decimal, and custom organization systems
  • 🔍 Smart Search: Full-text search with filters and saved searches
  • 📊 Analytics: Storage analysis, duplicate detection, and insights
  • 🔄 Undo/Redo: Reverse any operation instantly
  • 🎨 Multiple Interfaces: Web UI, CLI, and Terminal UI
  • 🔌 Extensible: Plugin system for custom functionality

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
File Organizer processes 43+ file formats including:

  • Documents: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Markdown, EPUB
  • Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF
  • Video: MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, WMV
  • Audio: MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG
  • Archives: ZIP, 7Z, TAR, RAR
  • Scientific: HDF5, NetCDF, MATLAB files
  • CAD: DXF, DWG, STEP, IGES

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.9+
  • RAM: 8 GB minimum (16 GB recommended)
  • Storage: ~10 GB for AI models
  • Ollama: Latest version for local inference

docs.title: Organize Files
docs.text:
file-organizer organize <input> <output> [OPTIONS]

Example:

file-organizer organize ./Downloads ./Organized

Options:

  • --methodology {para,johnny-decimal} - Organization system
  • --dry-run - Preview without moving files
  • --preserve - Keep originals
  • --verbose - Detailed output

docs.title: Search Files
docs.text:
file-organizer search <query> [OPTIONS]

Example:

file-organizer search "*.pdf"

docs.title: Deduplicate
docs.text:
file-organizer dedupe scan <path> [OPTIONS]

Example:

file-organizer dedupe scan ~/Documents

  • --port - Server port (default: 8000)

docs.title: What is File Organizer?
docs.text: File Organizer is an AI-powered local file management system that automatically organizes files using local LLMs (large language models). It supports multiple organization methodologies like PARA and Johnny Decimal, with zero cloud dependencies.

docs.title: Is my data safe?
docs.text:
Yes. File Organizer:

  • Runs 100% locally
  • Never uploads files to cloud
  • Uses local AI models
  • Keeps all data on your device

docs.title: What are the system requirements?
docs.text:
• Python: 3.9+
  • RAM: 8 GB minimum (16 GB recommended)
  • Storage: 10 GB for AI models
  • Ollama: Latest version

docs.title: Can I use it on Windows/Mac/Linux?
docs.text: Yes. File Organizer runs on all three platforms.

docs.title: How do I install File Organizer?
docs.text:
Three options:

  1. Docker (recommended): docker-compose up -d
  2. Python Package: pip install file-organizer
  3. From Source: Clone repo and pip install -e .

See Installation Guide.

docs.title: Do I need Ollama?
docs.text: Yes, Ollama provides the AI models. Install from https://ollama.ai

docs.title: Which AI models should I use?
docs.text:
We recommend:

  • Text: qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M (~1.9 GB)
  • Vision: qwen2.5vl:7b-q4_K_M (~6 GB)

Both are optimized for balance between speed and accuracy.

docs.title: How do I organize my files?
docs.text:
1. Upload files
  2. Click Organize
  3. Choose methodology (PARA, Johnny Decimal, etc.)
  4. Review preview
  5. Click Apply

See Organization Guide.

docs.title: What file types does it support?
docs.text:
File Organizer supports 43+ file types:

  • Documents: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Markdown
  • Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF
  • Video: MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, WMV
  • Audio: MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG
  • Archives: ZIP, 7Z, TAR, RAR
  • Scientific: HDF5, NetCDF, MATLAB
  • CAD: DXF, DWG, STEP, IGES

docs.title: How do I undo an organization?
docs.text:
Click Undo immediately after organizing (or Ctrl+Z).

Or use Organize → Original Structure to revert all organization.

docs.title: Can I organize files without uploading them?
docs.text: Yes. Click Organize → Browse Local Folder to organize files already on your system.

docs.title: How do I find duplicate files?
docs.text: Click Analysis → Detect Duplicates, choose folder(s) to scan, and wait for results.

docs.title: Getting Started with File Organizer
docs.text: This guide will help you install and set up File Organizer quickly.

docs.title: Installation Methods
docs.text:
Choose the installation method that best fits your needs:

Docker (Recommended) 
**Best for**: Production deployments, consistent environments

**Prerequisites**:
- Docker & Docker Compose installed
- 4GB+ available disk space

**Install**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/curdriceaurora/Local-File-Organizer.git
cd Local-File-Organizer
cp .env.example .env
docker-compose up -d
```

**Access**: Open browser to `http://localhost:8000/ui/`

See [Deployment Guide](admin/deployment.md) for detailed Docker setup.
Python Package 
**Best for**: Quick testing, simple deployments

**Prerequisites**:
- Python 3.9 or higher
- Ollama installed and running
- 4GB+ available disk space

**Install**:

```bash
pip install file-organizer
file-organizer serve
```

**Access**: Open browser to `http://localhost:8000/ui/`

See [Installation Guide](admin/installation.md) for options.
From Source 
**Best for**: Development, customization

**Prerequisites**:
- Python 3.9 or higher
- Git
- Ollama installed
- Development tools (C compiler)

**Install**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/curdriceaurora/Local-File-Organizer.git
cd file_organizer_v2
pip install -e .

# Pull required AI models
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M      # Text model
ollama pull qwen2.5vl:7b-q4_K_M             # Vision model

# Start the web server
file-organizer serve
```

**Access**: Open browser to `http://localhost:8000/ui/`

docs.title: Choosing an Organization Methodology
docs.text: File Organizer supports multiple organization systems:

docs.title: PARA (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives)
docs.text:
Best for: Knowledge workers, complex projects

Structure:

PARA/
├── Projects/        # Active projects with deadlines
├── Areas/           # Ongoing responsibilities
├── Resources/       # Reference materials
└── Archives/        # Completed projects

Learn more: PARA Guide

docs.title: Johnny Decimal
docs.text:
Best for: Hierarchical organization, fixed categories

Structure:

JD/
├── 10-19 Area 1/
│   ├── 11 Category A
│   ├── 12 Category B
├── 20-29 Area 2/
│   ├── 21 Category C

Learn more: Johnny Decimal Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide covers deploying File Organizer to production environments using Docker and standard web server practices.

docs.title: Docker Compose Setup
docs.text:
Create a docker-compose.yml file:

version: '3.8'

services:
  web:
    image: file-organizer:latest
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@db:5432/file_organizer
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis
      - ollama
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
      - ./uploads:/app/uploads

  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=user
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password
      - POSTGRES_DB=file_organizer
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data

  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:
  ollama_data:

docs.title: Generating an API Key
docs.text:
API keys are personal access tokens for API requests.

  1. Log in to web interface
  2. Click Settings (gear icon)
  3. Go to API Keys
  4. Click Generate New Key
  5. Configure:
  6. Name: Identify the key (e.g., "Python Script")
  7. Expiration: When key expires (30 days, 90 days, 1 year, never)
  8. Permissions: Select what key can do
  9. Click Generate
  10. Copy the token (shown only once)

docs.title: API Key Format
docs.text:
API keys are personal access tokens:

fo_abc123_token456
  • Prefix: fo_ (File Organizer)
  • ID: unique identifier
  • Token: secret portion
  • Unique per key

docs.text:

curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/files \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
API requests are rate-limited to prevent abuse.

Rate limits are configured in the application settings (ApiSettings).

  • Default Limit: 1000 requests/minute
  • Configurable: Administrators can adjust rate_limit_default_requests and rate_limit_rules.

docs.title: Checking Rate Limits
docs.text:
Rate limits appear in response headers:

X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1645026000
  • Limit: Total requests per minute
  • Remaining: Requests left in current window
  • Reset: Unix timestamp when window resets

docs.title: Handling Rate Limits
docs.text:
If you exceed the limit:

{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Too many requests",
    "retryAfter": 60
  }
}

Response:

  • HTTP Status: 429 Too Many Requests
  • Retry-After header indicates seconds to wait

Best Practices:

  • Wait before retrying
  • Use exponential backoff
  • Batch requests when possible
  • Consider upgrading tier

docs.title: Unauthorized (401)
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "UNAUTHORIZED",
    "message": "Invalid or missing API key"
  }
}

Causes:

  • Missing API key
  • Invalid API key
  • Expired API key
  • Revoked API key

Solutions:

  • Check key is included
  • Verify key format
  • Generate new key if expired
  • Check if key was revoked

docs.title: Forbidden (403)
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "FORBIDDEN",
    "message": "Permission denied",
    "details": {
      "required": "write:files",
      "granted": "read:files"
    }
  }
}

Causes:

  • Key lacks required permission
  • User lacks access to resource

Solutions:

  • Regenerate key with needed permissions
  • Use different key
  • Contact administrator

docs.title: Key Management
docs.text:
1. Keep Keys Secret

  2. Generate new keys periodically

# my_plugin.py
from file_organizer.plugins import Plugin, register_hook

class MyPlugin(Plugin):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.name = "my-plugin"
        self.version = "1.0.0"

        """Called when plugin is loaded"""
        register_hook("on_file_uploaded", self.on_upload)

        """Handle file upload"""
        print(f"File uploaded: {file.name}")

docs.title: Quick Search
docs.text:
Use the search bar at the top of any page:

docs.text:

docs.title: Saving Searches
docs.text:

docs.title: Advanced Search

docs.title: Search Query
docs.text:
Enter search terms using natural language:

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:

Operator Example Result type: type:pdf PDF files only size: size:>10mb Larger than 10 MB date: date:>2024-01 After Jan 2024 path: path:/documents In Documents folder tag: tag:important Tagged as important modified: modified:last7days Modified in last 7 days

Ignore

File organization is the process of:

  1. Analyzing files
  2. Categorizing them based on content
  3. Moving/renaming them into a structured hierarchy
  4. Applying consistent naming conventions

docs.title: Organization Methodologies
docs.text: File Organizer supports multiple systems:

docs.title: PARA Methodology
docs.text: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives - A flexible system for knowledge workers.

docs.title: PARA Structure
docs.text:
PARA/
├── Projects/           # Active projects with deadlines
│   ├── Website Redesign/
│   ├── Research Paper/
│   └── Product Launch/
├── Areas/              # Ongoing responsibilities
│   ├── Health/
│   ├── Finance/
│   └── Career/
├── Resources/          # Reference materials
│   ├── Templates/
│   ├── Tools/
│   └── Articles/
└── Archives/           # Completed items
    ├── 2023 Projects/
    └── Old Areas/

docs.title: PARA Organization Steps
docs.text:
1. Click Organize → PARA
  2. Select files
  3. Choose which category they fit:
  4. Projects: Time-bound initiatives
  5. Areas: Ongoing areas of life
  6. Resources: Reference material
  7. Archives: Completed/inactive
  8. AI analyzes content and suggests categories
  9. Review and confirm
  10. Click Apply

docs.title: PARA Best Practices
docs.text:
• Review projects quarterly
  • Archive completed items
  • Keep resources organized by type
  • Use consistent folder structure
  • Combine with tags for flexibility

docs.title: Johnny Decimal System
docs.text: JD is a hierarchical, numbered system. Perfect for structured organization.

docs.title: Johnny Decimal Structure
docs.text:
JD/
├── 10-19 Career/
│   ├── 11 CV & Applications/
│   ├── 12 Job Offers/
│   └── 13 Training & Development/
├── 20-29 Finance/
│   ├── 21 Taxes/
│   ├── 22 Invoices/
│   └── 23 Bank Statements/
├── 30-39 Health/
│   ├── 31 Medical Records/
│   ├── 32 Prescriptions/
│   └── 33 Fitness/
└── 40-49 Personal/
    ├── 41 Travel/
    ├── 42 Family/
    └── 43 Hobbies/

docs.title: Johnny Decimal Organization Steps
docs.text:
1. Click Organize → Johnny Decimal
  2. Select files
  3. Choose category (10-99)
  4. Choose subcategory
  5. Enter decimal number
  6. Review organization
  7. Click Apply

docs.title: Johnny Decimal Rules
docs.text:
• X0-X9: 10 main categories
  • X0-X9: 10 subcategories each
  • X.XX: File numbering within subcategory
  • Max 10 items per level
  • Simple, clear structure

docs.title: Johnny Decimal Best Practices
docs.text:
• Plan categories before starting
  • Keep similar items together
  • Use consistent naming
  • Don't skip numbers
  • Review structure regularly

docs.title: Custom Methodologies
docs.text: Create your own organization system.

docs.title: Creating Custom Rules
docs.text:
1. Click Organize → Custom
  2. Click Create New Rule
  3. Define rule:
  4. Name: Rule identifier
  5. Condition: What files match (e.g., type:pdf)
  6. Action: Where to put them
  7. Add more rules
  8. Test with Preview
  9. Apply when ready

docs.title: Rule Conditions
docs.text:
Match files by:

  • File Type: pdf, image, video, etc.
  • File Size: >10mb, \<1mb, etc.
  • Extension: .pdf, .docx, etc.
  • Date: Recent (last month, etc.)
  • Name: Pattern matching
  • Content: Keywords in file

docs.title: Rule Actions
docs.text:
Actions for matched files:

  • Move to Folder: Specific path
  • Rename: Pattern-based renaming
  • Tag: Add tags automatically
  • Copy: Keep original + copy
  • Archive: Move to archive folder

docs.title: Example Custom Rules
docs.text:
Rule 1: PDF Documents

  • Condition: type:pdf
  • Action: Move to Documents/PDFs/

Rule 2: Recent Photos

  • Condition: type:image AND date:>30days
  • Action: Move to Photos/Recent/

Rule 3: Large Files

  • Condition: size:>100mb
  • Action: Move to Archive/Large Files/

docs.title: Step 1: Select Files
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Organize
  2. Click Select Files
  3. Choose:
  4. Specific Files: Click individual files
  5. Folder: Select entire folder
  6. Search Results: Organize search results
  7. See count of selected files

docs.title: Step 2: Choose Methodology
docs.text:
1. Select methodology:
  2. PARA
  3. Johnny Decimal
  4. Custom
  5. None (undo previous)
  6. Configure options:
  7. Dry run (preview only)
  8. Preserve originals
  9. Create folders
  10. Apply metadata

docs.title: Step 3: Review Preview
docs.text:
1. See preview showing:
  2. Current location of each file
  3. Proposed new location
  4. Metadata changes
  5. Issues appear if any:
  6. Invalid paths
  7. Permission problems
  8. Naming conflicts
  9. Fix issues if needed

docs.title: Step 4: Apply Organization
docs.text:
1. Review looks good
  2. Click Apply
  3. Progress bar shows organization status
  4. See results when complete:
  5. Files organized
  6. Files skipped (and why)
  7. Any errors

docs.title: Dry Run (Preview Only)
docs.text:
See what would happen without actually organizing:

  1. Enable Dry Run
  2. Complete organization workflow
  3. See preview and results
  4. No files are moved
  5. Run again with Dry Run off to apply

docs.title: Preserve Originals
docs.text:
Keep original files while organizing:

  1. Enable Preserve Originals
  2. Files are copied (not moved)
  3. Originals remain in source folder
  4. Useful as backup

docs.title: Create Folders
docs.text:
Automatically create folder structure:

  1. Enable Create Folders
  2. Non-existent folders are created
  3. Avoids "file not found" errors
  4. Useful for new methodologies

docs.title: Apply Metadata
docs.text:
Extract and apply file metadata:

  1. Enable Apply Metadata
  2. AI extracts information
  3. Creates metadata files
  4. Updates file properties

docs.title: Job Progress
docs.text:
During organization:

  1. Progress bar shows % complete
  2. Current file being organized
  3. Estimated time remaining
  4. Speed (files/second)

docs.title: Pause & Resume
docs.text:
1. Click Pause to stop
  2. Work resumes where it left off
  3. Click Resume to continue
  4. Or click Cancel to stop entirely

docs.title: Job History
docs.text:
View past organization jobs:

  1. Click History
  2. See all past organization jobs
  3. Job details:
  4. Date/time started
  5. Files organized
  6. Methodology used
  7. Duration
  8. Click job to see details

docs.title: Immediate Undo
docs.text:
If you organize by mistake:

  1. Click Undo (or Ctrl+Z)
  2. Last operation is reversed
  3. All files return to original locations
  4. Original names restored

docs.title: Undo Limitations
docs.text:
• Can only undo recent operations
  • Undo history limited to ~20 operations
  • Cannot undo after server restart
  • For older changes, restore from backup

docs.title: Reverting Organization
docs.text:
To revert all organization:

  1. Click Organize
  2. Choose Original Structure
  3. Select organized files
  4. Click Apply
  5. Files return to original structure

docs.title: Scheduling Organization
docs.text: Automatically organize files on a schedule.

docs.title: Creating Schedule
docs.text:
1. Click Organize → Schedule
  2. Create new schedule:
  3. Name: Schedule name
  4. Folder: Watch this folder
  5. Methodology: Use this method
  6. Frequency: Daily/Weekly/Monthly
  7. Time: When to run
  8. Click Create

docs.title: Managing Schedules
docs.text:
1. View active schedules
  2. Pause/resume schedule
  3. Edit schedule settings
  4. See schedule results
  5. Delete when no longer needed

docs.title: Schedule History
docs.text:
View scheduled organization results:

  1. Click Schedule → History
  2. See all past runs
  3. Details for each run:
  4. Date/time
  5. Files organized
  6. Success/failures
  7. Export results if needed

docs.title: Before Organizing
docs.text:
• Backup: Make backup of important files
  • Review: Check files for duplicates
  • Plan: Decide on methodology first
  • Test: Use dry-run on small sample first

docs.title: During Organization
docs.text:
• Monitor: Watch progress
  • Avoid Edits: Don't modify files while organizing
  • Keep Power: Ensure system stays on
  • Good Connection: Stable network if remote

docs.title: After Organization
docs.text:
• Verify: Check organized files
  • Update: Update any shortcuts/links
  • Share: Let users know new locations
  • Document: Record organization decisions

docs.title: Files Not Organizing
docs.text:
• Check file permissions
  • Ensure destination folder exists
  • Verify methodology settings
  • Try dry-run to see issues

docs.title: Duplicates Found
docs.text:
• Review duplicates before organizing
  • Use duplicate detection to clean up
  • Decide which to keep
  • Then organize

docs.title: Slow Performance
docs.text:
• Organize in smaller batches
  • Close other applications
  • Use wired connection if possible
  • Check available disk space

docs.title: Settings & Configuration Guide
docs.text: Customize File Organizer to fit your workflow.

docs.title: Accessing Settings
docs.text: Click the gear icon (⚙️) in the top right corner, then select Settings.

docs.title: Workspace Path
docs.text:
Configure where File Organizer stores its data:

  1. Click Workspace → Path
  2. Choose workspace location
  3. Ensure sufficient disk space (10+ GB recommended)
  4. Click Save

Note: Changing workspace requires restart

docs.title: Workspace Name
docs.text:
Give your workspace a custom name:

  1. Click Workspace → Name
  2. Enter workspace name
  3. Click Save

Uses: Shown in web interface title and API responses

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
Choose light or dark theme:

  1. Click Appearance → Theme
  2. Select:
  3. Light mode
  4. Dark mode
  5. Auto (follows system)
  6. Changes apply immediately

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Select interface language:

  1. Click Appearance → Language
  2. Choose from:
  3. English
  4. Spanish
  5. French
  6. German
  7. Japanese
  8. (More coming soon)
  9. Interface updates immediately

docs.title: Display Density
docs.text:
Adjust interface spacing:

  1. Click Appearance → Density
  2. Choose:
  3. Compact (more content visible)
  4. Normal (default)
  5. Spacious (easier to read)
  6. Updates immediately

docs.title: Font Size
docs.text:
Adjust text size:

  1. Click Appearance → Font Size
  2. Choose from slider
  3. Updates immediately

docs.title: Notification Preferences
docs.text:
Control what notifications you receive:

  1. Click Notifications
  2. Toggle notification types:
  3. Job completion
  4. Errors and warnings
  5. System updates
  6. Tips and suggestions
  7. Click Save

docs.title: Desktop Notifications
docs.text:
Enable browser desktop notifications:

  1. Click Notifications → Desktop
  2. Grant permission when prompted
  3. Notifications appear even when tab inactive

docs.title: Notification Sound
docs.text:
Enable/disable notification sounds:

  1. Click Notifications → Sound
  2. Toggle on/off
  3. Test sound button available

docs.title: Generating API Keys
docs.text:
Create API tokens for programmatic access:

  1. Click API Keys
  2. Click Generate New Key
  3. Configure:
  4. Name: Identify the key
  5. Expiration: When key expires
  6. Permissions: What can be accessed
  7. Key is shown once - copy immediately
  8. Click Done

docs.title: Managing API Keys
docs.text:
View and manage your API keys:

For Each Key:

  • Name and creation date
  • Expiration date
  • Last used date
  • Copy token
  • Revoke: Delete immediately
  • Regenerate: Reset with new token

docs.title: API Key Permissions
docs.text:
Control what each API key can do:

  • Read Files: List and view files
  • Write Files: Upload and modify files
  • Organize: Start organization jobs
  • Analyze: Run analysis and search
  • Delete: Remove files
  • Admin: Full access (dangerous!)

docs.title: Default Methodology
docs.text:
Set default organization method:

  1. Click Organization → Default
  2. Choose:
  3. PARA
  4. Johnny Decimal
  5. Custom
  6. None
  7. Click Save

docs.title: Methodology Options
docs.text:
Configure methodology-specific settings:

PARA

  • Default folder structure
  • Auto-create subfolders

Johnny Decimal

  • Starting number range
  • Subfolder naming
  • Archiving rules

Custom

  • Save custom rules
  • Import/export rules
  • Create rule templates

docs.title: Organization Behavior
docs.text:
Control how organization works:

  1. Click Organization → Behavior
  2. Configure:
  3. Dry Run: Always preview first
  4. Preserve Originals: Keep copies
  5. Create Folders: Auto-create structure
  6. Auto-Backup: Backup before organizing
  7. Click Save

docs.title: Upload Limits
docs.text:
Configure file upload restrictions:

  1. Click Upload → Limits
  2. Set:
  3. Max file size (per file)
  4. Max batch size (total)
  5. Supported file types
  6. Click Save

docs.title: Auto-Scan
docs.text:
Enable automatic duplicate detection:

  1. Click Upload → Auto-Scan
  2. Toggle Enable Auto-Scan
  3. Configure:
  4. Scan after upload
  5. Similarity threshold
  6. Click Save

docs.title: Backup Settings
docs.text:
Configure file backups:

  1. Click Upload → Backups
  2. Configure:
  3. Keep backups before organizing
  4. Backup retention (days)
  5. Backup location
  6. Click Save

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
Update your account password:

  1. Click Security → Password
  2. Enter current password
  3. Enter new password (twice)
  4. Click Change Password

Password Requirements:

  • At least 8 characters
  • Mix of upper and lowercase
  • At least one number
  • At least one special character

docs.title: Two-Factor Authentication
docs.text:
Enable additional security:

  1. Click Security → 2FA
  2. Choose method:
  3. Authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.)
  4. SMS (if configured)
  5. Follow setup wizard
  6. Save backup codes (securely!)

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
View and manage active sessions:

  1. Click Security → Sessions
  2. See all active sessions:
  3. Browser type
  4. IP address
  5. Last activity
  6. Click Logout to end session
  7. Logout All to sign out everywhere

docs.title: Login History
docs.text:
Review recent login activity:

  1. Click Security → Login History
  2. See:
  3. Date and time
  4. IP address
  5. Browser and OS
  6. Success/failure

docs.title: Data Collection
docs.text:
Control what data is collected:

  1. Click Privacy → Data Collection
  2. Toggle options:
  3. Usage analytics
  4. Error reporting
  5. Feature suggestions
  6. No personal data is collected

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
Manage browser cookies:

  1. Click Privacy → Cookies
  2. See what cookies are used:
  3. Session management
  4. User preferences
  5. Analytics
  6. Clear cookies if desired

docs.title: Third-Party Services
docs.text:
View integrations:

  1. Click Privacy → Integrations
  2. No third-party integrations by default
  3. Enable if connecting external services

docs.title: View Storage
docs.text:
See storage usage breakdown:

  1. Click Storage → Usage
  2. See:
  3. Total capacity
  4. Used space
  5. Available space
  6. Breakdown by category

docs.title: Clean Up Storage
docs.text:
Free up disk space:

  1. Click Storage → Cleanup
  2. Options:
  3. Delete old backups
  4. Clear caches
  5. Archive old files
  6. Remove duplicates
  7. Preview what will be deleted
  8. Click Cleanup

docs.title: Storage Alerts
docs.text:
Get notified when storage runs low:

  1. Click Storage → Alerts
  2. Configure:
  3. Alert at % full (e.g., 80%)
  4. Notification method
  5. Click Save

docs.title: System Information
docs.text:
View system details:

  1. Click Advanced → System
  2. See:
  3. Python version
  4. Ollama version
  5. Database info
  6. Available RAM/CPU

docs.title: Import/Export
docs.text:
Backup and restore settings:

Export Settings

  1. Click Advanced → Import/Export
  2. Click Export Settings
  3. JSON file downloads

Import Settings

  1. Click Import Settings
  2. Choose JSON file
  3. Settings are restored

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Access application logs:

  1. Click Advanced → Logs
  2. Filter by level:
  3. Debug
  4. Info
  5. Warning
  6. Error
  7. View recent logs
  8. Download logs file

docs.title: Reset to Defaults
docs.text:
Reset all settings:

  1. Click Advanced → Reset
  2. Choose what to reset:
  3. All settings
  4. Workspace only
  5. User preferences
  6. WARNING: This cannot be undone
  7. Click Reset

docs.title: Responsive Mode
docs.text:
The web interface adapts to mobile:

  1. Settings accessible on mobile
  2. Same functionality as desktop
  3. Touch-optimized interface
  4. Reduced features on very small screens

docs.title: Offline Mode
docs.text:
Some features work offline:

  • View cached files
  • Read previous searches
  • Check settings (read-only)
  • No uploads/organization offline

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
Quick keyboard shortcuts in settings:

Shortcut Action / Focus search in settings Ctrl+S Save current setting Escape Close dialog

docs.title: Settings Not Saving
docs.text:
• Check for validation errors
  • Ensure sufficient disk space
  • Try browser refresh
  • Check browser cookies enabled

docs.title: API Key Not Working
docs.text:
• Verify key is copied correctly
  • Check key hasn't expired
  • Ensure key has required permissions
  • Regenerate key if needed

docs.title: 2FA Not Working
docs.text:
• Verify time sync on device
  • Check backup codes
  • Try different authenticator app
  • Contact administrator

docs.title: Backup Settings
docs.text:
Export all settings before major changes:

  1. Click Advanced → Export Settings
  2. Save JSON file
  3. Keep in secure location
  4. Can restore if needed
